value.string: count_only=False, limit=50, offset=0, query=None, relative_url=None, select_list=[], sort_on=None

Search the ERP5 catalog, either across the whole portal or inside one module.
 
 Omit relative_url and the search covers every module at once — the same
 catalog the UI's global search field queries. Name a module and it is that
 same catalog restricted to the module's contents, so scoping narrows, it
 never reaches anything a portal-wide search would miss.
 
 Results include each document's relative_url for further reading with erp5_read.
 
 QUERY SYNTAX: 'column:value' or 'column:"value with spaces"' — terms are
 ANDed, and the word AND between them is optional. Comparisons are
 understood: 'modification_date:>=2024-06-01 AND modification_date:<2024-07-01'
 becomes ONE range criterion, quoted or not. OR, NOT and parentheses cannot
 be mapped — the query is dropped whole and 'warning' says so, so do not
 write '( a AND b )'. Words with no column match title LIKE %words%, and
 only when no column term is present. 'filters_applied' echoes back what was
 really sent to the catalog.
 
 USE THIS WHEN:
 - You are looking for documents ACROSS modules — this is the only tool that
 can, by leaving relative_url out. erp5_collect always works inside one
 listbox.
 - You need to find documents by keyword, state, contributor, or other criteria.
 - You want a paginated list of documents in a module.
 - You need just a few fields per document (use select_list for efficiency).
 - You need HOW MANY documents match — pass count_only=true.
 
 DO NOT USE THIS WHEN:
 - You are filtering or reading a column the module SHOWS in its listbox, such
 as a related key like accounting_transaction_mirror_section_title
 ("Personenkonto") or a date like operation_date — use erp5_collect. This
 tool runs the plain catalog, so a module's own list_method and its
 default parameters are not applied: such a column comes back empty and a
 criterion on it either fails or is silently ignored. erp5_inspect lists
 those columns under search_columns.
 - You want the result a user sees in the module — use erp5_collect. Counts
 can differ legitimately, because the listbox applies default parameters
 (a section scope, for instance) that this tool knows nothing about.
 - You need ALL rows from a document's embedded listbox — use erp5_collect instead.
 - You want the full content of a single document — use erp5_read with its relative_url.
 - You need a document tree (e.g. Sale Order + all Lines) — use erp5_read_deep.
 
 NEXT STEPS: Use relative_url from results with erp5_read (single doc) or erp5_read_deep (tree).
 
 WATCH THE 'hint' AND 'warning' KEYS: when this tool notices it has hit a
 limit of the plain catalog path — a requested column empty in every row, or
 a join the catalog cannot make on its own — it returns 'hint' naming the
 tool to use instead. 'warning' means a criterion was not applied at all.
 Either way the rows may be unfiltered or incomplete, so read it before
 trusting them.
 
 COUNTING: pass count_only=true and read 'total_count'. That is one catalog
 COUNT query against the same filters the search itself would apply — exact,
 and independent of how many documents match. It returns no rows.
 
 Without count_only there is still no total: 'count' is the number of rows on
 the page you asked for, and 'has_more' is a heuristic (a full page came back,
 so more probably exist). DO NOT use limit=1 to count — it answers count=1
 whatever matches. Paging until has_more is false and summing 'count' also
 works, but costs one request per page and returns every row to do it.
